title: Which limit is it hitting?
starter:
let limit (peak : float) (bandwidth : float) (flops : float) (nbytes : float) : string =
  let intensity = nbytes /. flops in
  let memory_limit = peak *. intensity in
  if memory_limit < peak then "memory" else "compute"
hints: Intensity is FLOPs per byte. Which number goes on top of the division?
The memory limit is how fast memory can feed the kernel. Which of the machine's two numbers describes memory?
`let intensity = flops /. nbytes in` and `let memory_limit = bandwidth *. intensity in`. The last line is already right.

answer.code:
let limit (peak : float) (bandwidth : float) (flops : float) (nbytes : float) : string =
  let intensity = flops /. nbytes in
  let memory_limit = bandwidth *. intensity in
  if memory_limit < peak then "memory" else "compute"
answer.explain: Intensity is work per byte, so FLOPs go on top: 1 add per 12 bytes is 1/12, about 0.08. Memory feeds `bandwidth` times that many GFLOP/s. The first sample gets 25 / 12, about 2.1, far under the peak of 200, so memory is the limit. The second sample is the 768 by 768 matmul at 128 FLOPs per byte: memory could feed 3200 GFLOP/s, the processor only does 200, so compute is the limit.
